author: haiku
label: seeded-06-01
changes: Rewrote the file in the order: summary, terms, diagram, notes, failure table, open questions.
Split the request flow into an account branch and a rate-limit branch, so the reader sees that unknown addresses and over-limit requests create and send nothing.
Defined the reset_tokens fields and what the emailed link carries, so the link-click lookup is clear (Q4).
Stated that the rate limit counts per account from reset_tokens rows, and that count plus insert run in one locked transaction to hold the at-most-3 rule under concurrency (Q2).
Made the save step one transaction with a conditional token burn, so two submits and a half-failed save are both covered (Q7, Q8).
Stated that opening a link does not burn it, and that the used time is set only on save (Q7).
Added the failure table covering the request, link, save and worker failures (Q1, Q6, Q8).
Added open questions: Email queue location, an IP limit, a dropped email the user never learns of, and the cleanup rule for old reset_tokens rows (Q2, Q5, Q6).

Kept every stated brief rule: generic message, 3 per rolling hour, 32 random bytes, SHA-256 storage only, 30-minute expiry, single use, killing earlier unused links, 12-character minimum, breached-password check, link kept on password rejection, all sessions revoked, confirmation email, redirect to login without auto-login, and the worker's 3 retries.

Diagram A: the transaction now begins before the count, and its first step locks the account's users row. The count and the insert sit inside that transaction, so the file matches the rate-limit note (Q10).

Diagram A: the queue add is marked as in the transaction only if the queue is in Postgres. The failure table has separate rows for the queue-in-Postgres and queue-outside-Postgres cases, and the queue location is the first open question (Q13).
Diagram B and C: the GET page carries the raw token in a hidden field, and the POST sends it back (Q12).
Step 2 and the terms: stated that the mail job holds the raw token until it is sent or dropped, and raised this as an open question, because the brief's never-store rule may cover the queue (Q11).
Step 6 and rules: added what a logged-out device's next request sees, and noted that the brief does not set the response (Q15).
Rules: added the case of an older link opened after a newer one, and noted that the user is not told which email works (Q14).
Terms: added used time, transaction, row lock, conditional update, generic message and breached-password list, so that no term needs outside knowledge.

Restored the brief's exact generic message, the 12-character minimum with the breached-password list, the 3-per-rolling-hour limit, and the 'log out every device, including the one that did the reset, and do not log in automatically' rule, each in the step it applies to.
Failure table: added the old-link-opened row and the save-fails row now says the queue must be in Postgres for the rollback to cover the mail job.
Open questions: added the breached-password list source, the two-emails case and the confirmation-email case, and marked the queue question as the first open question.
Added a plain opening paragraph that says what the flow is, how the main flow runs, and why it has three parts.
Added a 'How it works today' paragraph that describes the existing API, Postgres, Email queue, worker and retry rule before the new design.

Expanded the terms so each is defined in one plain line. Added Email worker, Mail provider and Dead link, which the first version used without defining. Dead link is now a single term used in the steps.
Kept the diagram in its diagram form. Placed the summary and terms before it and the notes after it. The diagram content is unchanged except for the wording of the worker's retry line.
Moved the diagram's key facts into four short notes: raw token encoding, lock before count, hidden-field token, and used time set only on save.

Rewrote the six steps so each one states what starts it, what it does, what keeps its data, and what happens when it fails. Added the explicit token re-check on submit, the rate-limit no-row and no-email rule, and the 'does not start a session' rule from the brief.

Added short reasons in place: per-account limit (the brief sets it per account), lock before count (so two requests cannot both see 2), hidden field (no cookie or session needed), and rows kept (the rate-limit count needs them).
Merged the Rules section into one list of seven rules. Removed the repeated restatements of the same rules that were in the steps.
Kept all 12 rows of the failure table, with the same outcomes, reworded in plain words.
Kept all 8 open questions, including the queue location, the raw token in the queue, the IP limit, the dropped emails, the cleanup rule and the breached-list source.

Cut no stated fact. Every requirement in the brief and the first version is still present, including the generic message text, the 3-per-hour limit, the 30-minute single-use link, the hash-only storage, the 12-character and breached-list rules, the all-device logout, and the redirect without login.
Did not change the design. The one open point, whether the queue sits inside Postgres, is still listed as an open question and not decided.
holes: Q5: Does 'respond' wait for the email to be sent, or only for it to be put on the Email queue? What does the Email queue run on? (author: The brief says the API adds a job to the Email queue and the worker sends it, so the response waits only for the job to be added, not for the send. The brief does not say what the Email queue runs on, so that is unknown. It is an open question in the file.)

Q13: The failure table says that if the queue add fails the transaction rolls back and no link exists, but an open question says the queue may be outside Postgres and unable to share the transaction. Which one applies today, and what happens in each case? (author: The brief does not say where the Email queue runs. The file's design assumes it is in Postgres, so that the queue add rolls back with the transaction, and it says so in the diagram and the failure table. If the queue is outside Postgres, the rollback cannot cover it: the link row and burned old links are committed, and the email may never be queued. Which case applies today is not known. It is the first open question.)
